text.title: Spring Boot Layered Architecture Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules grounding the canonical layered Spring Boot 3 pattern. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Controllers MUST return Java record DTOs (`public record UserResponse(...)`); they MUST NOT return JPA entities. Mapping happens via MapStruct generated mappers inside the service layer.
rule.rationale: Returning entities leaks Hibernate proxy state, lazy associations, and internal schema; `@JsonIgnore` patches the symptom, not the cause.

rule.statement: Every service method that performs writes MUST be annotated `@Transactional`. Class-level `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` is the default; write methods override locally.
rule.rationale: Without `@Transactional` on multi-step writes, each JDBC call auto-commits; a partial failure leaves the database inconsistent with no rollback.

rule.statement: Every list endpoint MUST accept `Pageable` and return `Page<DTO>` (or `Slice`). `findAll()` without `Pageable` on growable tables is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Unbounded `findAll()` causes OOM and timeouts as tables grow; `Pageable` enforces a contract that callers paginate.

rule.statement: Passwords MUST be hashed via `PasswordEncoder` (BCrypt) inside the service layer. Controllers MUST NOT accept pre-hashed passwords from the client.
rule.rationale: Client-supplied hashes let an attacker replay an old hash; server-side hashing centralises the cost factor + algorithm choice.

rule.statement: `pom.xml` (or `build.gradle`) MUST configure the MapStruct annotation processor. Hand-coded DTO ↔ entity mappers are forbidden — they drift silently from the schema.
rule.rationale: Annotation-processor mappers fail at compile when a property goes missing; hand-coded mappers leak old field names into runtime.

rule.statement: Spring Boot 3 imports MUST be `jakarta.*` (`jakarta.persistence`, `jakarta.validation`). `javax.persistence` / `javax.validation` imports are forbidden in a Boot 3 codebase.
rule.rationale: Boot 3 migrated to Jakarta EE 9+ namespaces; mixing `javax.*` produces compile errors or — worse — silent runtime failures when both jars are on the classpath.

rule.statement: A controller method MUST accept the HTTP request, call exactly one service method, and return the response. `@Transactional`, repository access, business logic and multi-service orchestration in a controller are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Thin controllers keep `@WebMvcTest` + a mocked service sufficient to test the HTTP contract, and stop the layer bleed that makes a service impossible to reuse from a scheduler or a message consumer.

rule.statement: `@Transactional` (and `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`) MUST live on `@Service` methods or the service class. It MUST NOT appear on a controller, a repository, or a private method.

rationale.source: Spring transaction docs + Spring AOP docs

rule.rationale: A transaction on the controller ties the DB lifetime to the whole HTTP request including serialisation — open-in-view by another name — and holds row locks for the duration. On a private method the proxy never applies it, so the annotation silently does nothing.

rule.statement: Request DTOs MUST be Java `record` types carrying Bean Validation annotations (`@NotNull`, `@Size`, `@Email`, `@Positive`) and MUST be bound with `@Valid` at the controller. Response DTOs MUST be records carrying no logic. Service public methods MUST accept and return DTOs, never JPA entities.

rationale.source: Java 17 records spec + Bean Validation 3.x docs

rule.rationale: Records give value semantics and immutability for free; validating at the boundary keeps the domain free of defensive checks and produces a uniform 400 before any service code runs.

rule.statement: `@Async` methods MUST live in a bean separate from the caller — never self-invoked — and MUST name their executor (`@Async("emailExecutor")`) backed by a `ThreadPoolTaskExecutor` bean with explicit core size, max size and queue capacity.

rationale.source: Spring Async docs + observed self-invocation antipattern

rule.rationale: Self-invocation bypasses the AOP proxy so the method runs synchronously on the request thread, and the default `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` spawns an unbounded thread per call. Full treatment: [[java-spring-async]].
